I think that the main difference is that the Dreamer's projections have a bit more oomph than the Idealist's extensions-of-self.

The Dreamer is a massively powerful psychic at the conflux of a time/space tear.  She is putting out enough energy to rip the universe apart and put it back together again.  As such, her creations are so real that they can do toxic/melee/whatever damage.  They are infused with reality, pulled from actual events and altered by her perceptions.  To the dreamer, the nightmares ARE real.

The idealist is the memory of a girl, given form by a machine and sustained by belief.  When she creates something, she doesn't believe that its "real".  Its a construct karate robot, or floating knives, or a giant fist punching something.  and when it hits, it makes the opponent believe that they've taken damage.

According to the records of the time, they would appear in numerous guises, often as an animal, but also at times as a human or humanoid figure, and were described as "clearly defined, three-dimensional forms
